conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
RAOULT'S LAW VAPOUR PRESSURE EQUATION

P_total = p_A + p_B = p°_A x_A + p°_B x_B = p°_A + (p°_B - p°_A) x_B
conceptBreakdown.content:
For a solution of two volatile liquids A and B, the partial vapor pressure of each component is proportional to its mole fraction in liquid solution:
$$p_A = p_A^\circ x_A \quad \text{and} \quad p_B = p_B^\circ x_B$$
$$\mathbf{P_{\text{total}} = p_A^\circ x_A + p_B^\circ x_B = p_A^\circ + (p_B^\circ - p_A^\circ) x_B}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Vapour Phase Mole Fractions & Harmonic Relation
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Vapour Phase Mole Fractions & Harmonic Relation
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
VAPOUR PHASE COMPOSITION (DALTON'S LAW)

• y_A = p_A / P_total = (p°_A x_A) / P_total
• y_B = p_B / P_total = (p°_B x_B) / P_total

• Dalton-Raoult Harmonic Relation:
  1 / P_total = y_A / p°_A + y_B / p°_B
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Vapor Phase Mole Fractions ($y_A, y_B$)**: By Dalton's law of partial pressures, $p_A = y_A P_{\text{total}} \implies y_A = \frac{p_A^\circ x_A}{P_{\text{total}}}$.
• The more volatile component (higher $p^\circ$) is always enriched in the vapor phase ($y_A > x_A$ if $p_A^\circ > p_B^\circ$).

quickRevision: Vapor is richer in the more volatile component.
